content.text:
None of these intermediate commits touched the `Biweekly.write(ical).go()` call or added timezone configuration to the writer - confirming the pattern remained unchanged from `93de21ca` until the fix in `80dcd036`.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 93de21ca4af4279d8ac132e05a7692a7b75730f5

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit (`80dcd036`) changes four files from calling the convenience `Biweekly.write(ical).go()` method to manually constructing an `ICalWriter` and explicitly calling `writer.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(TimeZone.getDefault())` before serializing. Since the bug is about the biweekly iCal writer not being told which timezone to use when writing, I searched for when `Biweekly.write(...)`/`import biweekly.Biweekly` was first introduced in each of the four affected files. All four files picked up this import and pattern in a single commit, `93de21ca4af4279d8ac132e05a7692a7b75730f5` ("migrate to biweekly library"), and no other commit between then and the fix touched this writing logic.

**(2) Specific change:** `93de21ca` replaced the previous hand-rolled iCal text generation (which manually wrote `BEGIN:VCALENDAR`/date lines using `TimeZone.getDefault()` directly into the text, e.g. `X-WR-TIMEZONE:`+TimeZone.getDefault().getID()`) with the `biweekly` library. In this migration, `DateStart`/`DateEnd` properties are tagged with `setTimezoneId(TimeZone.getDefault().getID())`, but the actual `ICalWriter`/`Biweekly.write()` call used to serialize the calendar was never configured with a corresponding `TimezoneInfo`/default timezone. This mismatch means biweekly doesn't know how to resolve the TZID into an actual `VTIMEZONE` definition, so exported `.ics` times come out wrong (e.g., defaulting to UTC) — exactly the symptom the later fix corrects by explicitly setting `writer.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(TimeZone.getDefault())` at the point of writing.

**(3) Evidence:** `git log -S "import biweekly.Biweekly"` on all four files shows the import/pattern was added only in `93de21ca`, and the diff of that commit shows the old, correct manual timezone-aware date writing being torn out and replaced with biweekly calls lacking writer-level timezone configuration. I also confirmed none of the ~15 intermediate commits touching these files between `93de21ca` and `80dcd036` modified the write/timezone logic, so the defect persisted unchanged until the fix.

I'm fairly confident in this attribution since it's a single, well-isolated migration commit touching exactly the four files fixed, with a clear causal mechanism (missing writer-level timezone configuration) matching the fix precisely.
